title: Soundscaper editing responsiveness implementation register
scope: 100 audited Soundscaper editing responsiveness and processing-throughput candidates, with implementation dispositions. Startup/lazy loading and Framescaper-only features excluded; default Electron Speed preference verified.
interpretation: Proposal text, source locations and original measurements describe baseRevision. status and implementation describe the resulting changes and their tested admission limits. implemented means the bounded change is present; partial means narrower work landed with the stated remainder; rejected means no optimization landed, because measured regression or the current reviewed model/runtime/custody protocol does not support an adapter-only implementation. It does not prove every architectural proposal intrinsically invalid. Helper timings are not Electron or model-workflow speedups.

findings.title: Index looped clips for boundary snapping
findings.observedWork: Every snap query traverses every track clip ID to discover loop boundaries, including documents with no loops. Move snapping runs this scan for both edges. The existing sorted edge index only bounds the normal edge lookup.
findings.proposedChange: Store loop-bearing clips and track IDs in BoundarySnapIndex; query only indexed loop extents intersecting the pointer's tolerance window.
findings.scenario: Move or range-select in a 10,000-100,000-clip project, with snapping active.
findings.validation: Membership iterations per pointer update, handler CPU time, p95 drag frame interval; preserve coincident-boundary and exclusion behavior.
findings.existingProtection: Clip/source map lookups and normal boundary binary searches already exist; do not redo them.
findings.measurement: Membership-read fixture: 50,000 clipIds reads and 5,000,000 memberships across 500 indexed queries on 10,000 loop-free clips. Larger 100,000-clip fixture, 100 queries: median 373.49 ms over five trials after warm-up; 10,000,000 memberships. Moving a clip resolves two edges. Node work probe, not Electron drag FPS.

implementation.change: Retain loop-bearing extent queries and track endpoint indexes for boundary snapping.
implementation.proof: boundary-snap-performance tests and scripts/performance/measure-timeline-work.mjs observe zero hot-query clipIds reads and membership traversals; 100,000 clips / 100 queries warmed median 0.165ms in the focused Node probe.
implementation.limits: Index construction still visits the immutable project once; Node probe is not Electron drag FPS.

findings.title: Index microfade neighbors and collision intervals
findings.observedWork: After a successful edge snap, microfadeOverlapFrames materializes every destination-track clip, filters for the one touching neighbor, then scans all clips for collisions. A dense destination track repeats this cost as a clip stays snapped while dragging.
findings.proposedChange: Extend the immutable snap index with per-track start/end neighbor maps and a bounded interval collision query.
findings.scenario: Drag one audio clip around a dense track with applyMicrofadesToNewClips enabled.
findings.validation: Destination clip property reads and allocations per successful snapped move; p95 snapped-handler duration.
findings.existingProtection: The existing implementation already avoids project.clips.find through clipById; remaining work is scanning destination geometry.

implementation.change: Query touching neighbors and collisions through per-track endpoint maps and a maximum-end interval index.
implementation.proof: boundary-snap-performance tests bound hot dense-track neighbor geometry reads below 10 and preserve collision/exclusion cases.
implementation.limits: Dense overlapping collision results still cost proportional to actual intersecting neighbors.

findings.title: Coalesce canvas invalidations across React commits
findings.observedWork: Each changed layout-effect dependency immediately calls draw(), before paint. Several visual publications or selection commits within one display frame can repeat DOM scanning and draw-key construction even where unchanged canvases skip painting.
findings.proposedChange: Keep a persistent dirty renderer and latest-input ref, coalesce updates once per animation frame, and retain an explicit immediate path where first-frame correctness requires it.
findings.scenario: Multitrack recording publications, spectral tile completions, or rapidly changing selection.
findings.validation: Renderer scans/draws per display frame and main-thread time until the next paint; check no blank initial waveform.
findings.existingProtection: ResizeObserver redraws already use createAnimationFrameCoalescer and canvas draw keys already skip identical paint; this concerns dependency-driven synchronous draws.

implementation.change: Retain one waveform animation-frame scheduler and its observer across commits, reading the latest paint closure.
implementation.proof: 12 focused canvas/row/cache tests pass, including actual cached initial mount and virtualized remount without media publications, one total attachment retry per explicit draw, ref/host replacement, stale callback rejection, unmount and StrictMode reacquisition; existing scale/zoom raster and independent cache eviction protections still pass.
implementation.limits: Committed row changes paint at the next display frame. Initial parent-host attachment receives one cancellable frame retry; a still-absent host waits for another explicit invalidation.

findings.title: Batch waveform geometry and palette reads before canvas writes
findings.observedWork: The renderer reads one canvas rectangle, mutates backing dimensions and dataset/style, reads computed styles, paints, then reads the next canvas rectangle. Mixed reads and writes can trigger repeated style/layout work across clips.
findings.proposedChange: Collect live canvases, geometry, and theme/color palette first; then size and paint them in a write phase, caching palettes by theme/color revision.
findings.scenario: Zoom, resize, or selection paint across many visible clips at high DPI.
findings.validation: Forced layout/style-recalculation events and duration in an Electron trace; canvas paint CPU per frame.
findings.existingProtection: Canvas paint caching and bounded backing dimensions remain; this candidate is also acknowledged in performance-candidates.md and still needs a representative trace.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed read/write sequence; layout impact unmeasured

implementation.change: Apply canvas styles together, then collect all geometry/palettes before backing writes and painting.
implementation.proof: canvas-paint-measurements tests verify palette snapshot ownership and geometry/read ordering; existing raster fixtures preserve scale/zoom pixels.
implementation.limits: Layout still must be read when the viewport geometry changes.

findings.title: Paint selection with cached waveform layers
findings.observedWork: Selection pixel endpoints are part of the draw key. Every changed selection clears the complete clip and redraws all waveform columns in selected/unselected colors, although PCM geometry and envelope have not changed.
findings.proposedChange: Retain unselected and selected-color waveform images, and composite clipped selection regions plus body fill; invalidate these images only on geometry/audio/theme changes.
findings.scenario: Drag a time selection across a long visible stereo waveform.
findings.validation: Waveform column evaluations versus selection-only drawImage calls, p95 selection frame time, bounded cache bytes.
findings.existingProtection: Waveform plans and spectrogram raster images are already cached; selection currently changes the full waveform paint, not its analysis.

implementation.change: Cache bounded base/full-selected summary waveform layers and redraw only fractional selection-edge columns.
implementation.proof: Chromium waveform-selection-layers spec compares 448 exact RGBA images across stereo, translucent palettes, fractional selection, RMS, half-wave and dB scales. A 1,000-column selection move reads four extrema rather than 2,000. Cold fully-selected 1,000-column canvases now read 2,000 extrema instead of 4,000, render/copy/clear one initial layer instead of two, and lazily acquire the base only when needed. Chromium 512 exact RGBA cases pass, including cold full selections and existing transitions; hot full selections read 0 and fractional moves read 4. Raw operation counts and pixel cases are retained in the implementation measurements.
implementation.limits: Admitted only for regular summary waveforms at unit horizontal backing scale; sample/frequency/scaled modes retain exact original rendering. Shared retained pixels bounded to32MiB.

findings.title: Memoize unaffected mounted audio rows with narrow inputs
findings.observedWork: AudioTrackRow receives the full snapshot as viewModelRevision and freshly bound per-row callbacks. It is not memoized, so parent viewport, selection, or unrelated document changes still execute unchanged row render functions and their hooks.
findings.proposedChange: Pass stable track-specific visual revisions and callbacks, separate exact viewport/ruler ownership, and add memo boundaries with explicit relevant props.
findings.scenario: Many visible tracks while editing one track, opening a menu, or scrolling within an existing render anchor.
findings.validation: React Profiler unchanged-row render/commit counts and render duration, while exercising selection and recording changes.
findings.existingProtection: Expensive waveform view models are memoized and use a render anchor; telemetry selectors already isolate meters. This targets remaining row React work and is an existing unmeasured candidate.

implementation.change: Memoize heavy mounted audio rows behind row-local selection/drag sets, stable committed callback delegates and visible media tokens.
implementation.proof: audio-track-row-props tests retain identical props through 100 unrelated snapshot/selection/drag/callback updates, read one visible media clip rather than10,000, and preserve own/incoming invalidations and committed event ownership. Anchored viewport guard passes.
implementation.limits: Authoritative project/navigation inputs still invalidate rows when their own values change.

findings.title: Construct virtualized row children only when mounted
findings.observedWork: TrackListView calls renderTrack for every nonhidden track before TrackViewportRow decides whether to discard the resulting child element. Offscreen slots avoid heavy component execution, but parent construction of props, callbacks, and recording-preview searches still scales with all tracks.
findings.proposedChange: Provide a stable deferred row factory or move track-child creation into the mounted slot owner.
findings.scenario: A thousand-track project undergoing repeated scroll or selection updates.
findings.validation: Offscreen row-element constructions/allocations per update and parent render CPU.
findings.existingProtection: Mounted-row virtualization, shared IntersectionObserver, focus pinning, and accessible placeholder rows already exist; preserve them. Existing performance-candidates.md recognizes this remaining work.

implementation.change: Defer virtualized track child construction until the row mounts.
implementation.proof: track-viewport-factory tests verify offscreen child factories are not called and focus-navigation fallback remains reachable.
implementation.limits: Track planning and placeholder shells remain mounted for geometry/navigation.

findings.title: Window label markers horizontally
findings.observedWork: A mounted label track maps every label into a full interactive marker even when almost all labels are outside the time viewport.
findings.proposedChange: Index point/range labels against the viewport and render visible/overscan markers plus the active edit/focus marker; retain list-wide keyboard navigation.
findings.scenario: An imported annotation/label track with tens of thousands of points or regions.
findings.validation: Mounted label DOM count, zoom/selection React duration, p95 scroll frame interval.
findings.existingProtection: Audio/video clip viewports already bound their heavy content; label marker rendering does not share that bound.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed unbounded marker count; impact unmeasured

implementation.change: Index dense label markers and project only the anchored horizontal window plus selected/edited labels.
implementation.proof: label-viewport-model tests preserve order/retained IDs and perform zero geometry reads over10,000 indexed labels during window queries.
implementation.limits: Small label sets use the ordinary path; the window includes the existing128CSS-pixel text allowance and viewport overscan.

findings.title: Include label tracks in vertical row virtualization
findings.observedWork: The vertical virtualizer explicitly returns label rows directly. Every label track remains mounted below/above the viewport, including all of its markers and their listeners.
findings.proposedChange: Use TrackViewportRow for label rows with label-aware focus/edit pinning and placeholders.
findings.scenario: Large projects with many independently imported label tracks.
findings.validation: Offscreen label component/DOM counts, retained heap and vertical scrolling frame time.
findings.existingProtection: Audio/video rows already virtualize only in sessions over 24 tracks; preserve accessibility and active label edit state when generalizing it.

implementation.change: Put label tracks behind the same vertical TrackViewportRow owner as audio/video tracks.
implementation.proof: track-viewport-factory tests cover deferred label child factories, placeholder track attributes and navigation mounting.
implementation.limits: Rows remain discoverable through placeholder attributes; selected/focused rows keep existing mounting rules.

findings.title: Coalesce ordinary pointer preview work to display frames
findings.observedWork: Pinch zoom commits, track resize, selection, loop, stretch, and trim update previews/actions at raw pointer event rate. A 120-240 Hz pointer can drive more expensive projection/React work than the display can present.
findings.proposedChange: Keep the latest pointer sample/session result and publish once per animation frame; flush the latest canonical geometry on pointer-up and cancel stale scheduled work.
findings.scenario: High-polling mouse or touch drag of a selection, track edge, or clip trim.
findings.validation: Preview publications/action invocations per display frame, input-to-paint p95 and missed frames.
findings.existingProtection: Fade/crossfade previews already have RAF coalescing and ordinary move uses a small value-equality guard. Preserve those rather than claiming they are absent.

implementation.change: Coalesce ordinary timeline pointer drafts once per frame and flush the final pending move before committing.
implementation.proof: animation-frame-coalescer and timeline-pointer-frame tests cover latest movement, stale gesture rejection, final flush and Escape discard; immediate touch/pencil/fade paths preserve their existing contracts.
implementation.limits: At most one display-frame draft delay for admitted ordinary pointer tools; final commit is synchronous after flush.

findings.title: Use a maintained lane geometry table for pointer hit testing
findings.observedWork: Track targeting queries every lane and reads rectangles until finding the destination; range selection reads every lane rectangle on each move. Placeholder virtualized rows are still included, so these DOM reads can scale with total track count.
findings.proposedChange: Maintain row top/height prefix geometry invalidated by track resize/folder/dock changes, transform clientY through current scroll, and binary-search the destination/span. Reuse measured container bounds within a frame.
findings.scenario: Move clips vertically or drag a range across a thousand-track session.
findings.validation: getBoundingClientRect calls and lane iterations per event, forced layouts, p95 gesture CPU.
findings.existingProtection: Project clip/track indexes optimize document lookup; they do not index DOM lane geometry. Keep captured pointer and scrolling behavior covered.

implementation.change: Maintain indexed audio/label lane content geometry with explicit resize/mutation invalidation and current root/scroll translation.
implementation.proof: timeline-lane-index tests use10,000 lanes with one hot root geometry read; Chromium lane-geometry spec observes zero row rectangle reads over100 hits plus scroll and refreshes200rows after synchronous height invalidation.
implementation.limits: A real geometry change rebuilds the affected root table; ResizeObserver and MutationObserver own lifecycle cleanup.

findings.title: Patch only affected track projections during drag
findings.observedWork: Any clipDragPreview invalidates every mounted row's clip collection, copies/filter-scans its complete track, and disables the viewport clip index even for rows unrelated to the move. Large static tracks therefore fall back to full projection scans during a drag elsewhere.
findings.proposedChange: Compute affected source/destination track IDs once, retain unchanged row collections/indexes, and query the stable viewport index before applying a small dragged-clip overlay/exclusion.
findings.scenario: Move one clip while other visible tracks each hold thousands of clips.
findings.validation: Static-track clip reads/copies per move and p95 drag frame CPU; verify clips entering/leaving the viewport and cross-track previews.
findings.existingProtection: Static scroll projections already use an index above 128 clips; drag currently opts out globally. This is additional incremental drag ownership, not replacing the existing index.

implementation.change: Retain canonical clip viewport indexes across unrelated drags and overlay only incoming/outgoing row previews.
implementation.proof: track-drag-projection-performance tests retain a1,000-clip unrelated row projection with zero geometry reads and include offscreen incoming/removal cases.
implementation.limits: Affected source and destination rows still recompute their preview overlays.

findings.title: Skip RMS reductions when RMS is hidden
findings.observedWork: drawSummaryColumns reads every source RMS value and squares/adds it before checking showRms. Ordinary waveforms with RMS disabled still perform this work, including three frequency-band passes.
findings.proposedChange: Guard RMS reads and accumulation with showRms && channel.rms, leaving extrema unchanged.
findings.scenario: Zoom or select across many summary waveforms with Show RMS disabled.
findings.validation: RMS element reads and summary-render CPU; numerical/screenshot parity for both toggle states.
findings.existingProtection: The actual RMS paint and sqrt are already skipped when disabled; only its source reduction remains.
findings.measurement: Fake-canvas operation probe: 1,000 RMS reads for 1,000 columns while showRms=false. CPU/paint gains unmeasured.

implementation.change: Skip RMS array reductions when no RMS overlay is drawn.
implementation.proof: waveform-paint-performance tests and work probe observe zero hidden RMS reads across1,000 waveform columns.
implementation.limits: RMS remains reduced whenever it contributes visible pixels.

findings.title: Avoid repeated canvas fill-style assignments across uniform waveform runs
findings.observedWork: Every min/max column assigns fillStyle, even while the complete waveform uses the same base color. Selected waveforms generally have only three color runs; RMS-on alternation also prevents simple style reuse.
findings.proposedChange: Draw min/max and RMS as separate passes or color runs and set style once per run, preserving physical-pixel alignment and layering.
findings.scenario: Wide stereo summary canvases and three-band waveforms.
findings.validation: fillStyle setter count and canvas CPU per 1,000 columns; verify RMS compositing and selected colors.
findings.existingProtection: Physical-pixel boundary rounding already prevents fractional-width seams; this must be retained.

implementation.change: Retain canvas fill style across uniform waveform columns and switch only when a visible style changes.
implementation.proof: waveform-paint-performance tests preserve command geometry/color transitions while reducing repeated style writes; isolated Node drawing counters cover1,000columns.
implementation.limits: Selection/clipping/color changes intentionally switch styles.

findings.title: Batch connecting-dot and sample-stem paths by color
findings.observedWork: Connecting-dot mode begins and strokes a separate path for every adjacent pair; stem mode also strokes each sample individually. Most ordinary waveform samples share a color.
findings.proposedChange: Batch same-color segments/stems into paths, with separate groups at selection/color boundaries; validate joins/caps and rainbow rendering before adopting.
findings.scenario: Sample-level zoom into a visible mono/stereo clip.
findings.validation: stroke calls, canvas CPU and p95 zoom/selection paint; screenshot parity at joins and selection boundaries.
findings.existingProtection: Sample plans are already bounded; the remaining per-sample canvas call overhead is within that bound.
findings.correctness: Keep each original segment as a separate subpath where necessary and verify line caps, joins, clipping and overlapping alpha/compositing. A continuous polyline can change rendered pixels.
findings.measurement: Fake-canvas operation probe: 1,999 stroke calls for 2,000 connecting-dot samples. Actual painting/compositing gain unmeasured.

implementation.change: Batch disjoint sample stems by contiguous color at unit canvas scale while retaining individual sample-head caps.
implementation.proof: Chromium column-opacity spec checks192exact RGBA combinations across backing densities, widths, translations, half/dB scale and translucency. Admitted1,000stem drawing uses two strokes including center rather than1,001.
implementation.limits: Broad scaled/connecting-dot compound paths were rejected after exact-pixel experiments showed Skia anti-alias/overlap mismatches. Connecting dots and non-unit transforms retain individual strokes.

findings.title: Reuse sample coordinate scratch instead of allocating point objects per paint
findings.observedWork: Every individual-sample redraw creates a new array and one {x,y} object per sample, followed by multiple traversals.
findings.proposedChange: Stream previous/current coordinates for connecting dots and retain bounded numeric scratch for stems/heads when a second pass is needed.
findings.scenario: Repeated selection/envelope edits at sample zoom across multiple clips.
findings.validation: Allocated objects/bytes per redraw and GC pauses, with exact coordinate parity.
findings.existingProtection: The waveform planner already bounds sample count, so quantify allocation before prioritizing this P3 candidate.

implementation.change: Stream individual sample line coordinates directly and retain reusable frequency-band height scratch.
implementation.proof: waveform-paint-performance and frequency-waveform-renderer tests preserve recorded command geometry without per-sample point objects.
implementation.limits: Existing sample values and connecting-dot stroke order remain exact.

findings.title: Draw three-band RMS directly without a transparent peak pass
findings.observedWork: Three-band RMS requests the complete ordinary waveform renderer with sampleColor='transparent'. The renderer still evaluates extrema, writes fillStyle, and issues transparent min/max rectangles before drawing RMS.
findings.proposedChange: Add an explicit RMS-only paint mode that retains clipping to waveform extrema but omits transparent peak canvas writes.
findings.scenario: Three-band waveform mode with RMS enabled.
findings.validation: Peak fillRect calls eliminated per channel and canvas CPU; compare RMS envelope/extrema clipping pixels.
findings.existingProtection: Frequency analysis and palette caches already exist; this candidate only removes an unnecessary paint pass.

implementation.change: Paint three-band RMS directly with drawPeaks disabled instead of a transparent peak pass.
implementation.proof: frequency-waveform-renderer tests preserve visible RMS geometry and clipping detection while eliminating the hidden peak fills.
implementation.limits: Peak extrema remain available where needed to detect clipping.

findings.title: Keep ruler and grid backing buffers when dimensions are unchanged
findings.observedWork: Both canvases assign width and height on every redraw, even for selection-only or scroll-only changes. Canvas dimension assignment clears/resets the drawing context and can recreate backing resources despite unchanged geometry.
findings.proposedChange: Compare backing dimensions before assignments and otherwise clear/repaint the existing buffer; keep ratio/theme invalidation explicit.
findings.scenario: Pinned playback, horizontal scrolling, or selection drag with musical/timecode rulers.
findings.validation: Backing-dimension writes/resource allocations per scroll frame and paint CPU.
findings.existingProtection: Both canvases are viewport-sized and have a dimension ceiling; normal clip canvases already compare dimensions before writes.

implementation.change: Resize timeline ruler/grid backing buffers only when dimensions change.
implementation.proof: timeline-shared-ticks/grid/ruler tests preserve fractional positioning and existing backing geometry.
implementation.limits: True size/DPR changes still clear and resize buffers.

findings.title: Share viewport tick generation between rulers and grid canvases
findings.observedWork: Mapped ruler drawing builds musical/timecode ticks, and grid-line generation separately calls the same tick generators for the same sample-rate/zoom/viewport. Output-dock grids can repeat the same preparation.
findings.proposedChange: Resolve an immutable viewport tick model once at its owning timeline and pass/project it into ruler and all grid paints.
findings.scenario: Scrolling a musical tempo-map project or timecode project with output lanes open.
findings.validation: Tick-builder calls and allocations per viewport change, preserving exact tick/grid alignment.
findings.existingProtection: Grid lines are memoized and painted as two batched paths; this concerns repeated tick-model construction across consumers.

implementation.change: Generate mapped viewport ticks once and pass them to ruler, grid and output canvases.
implementation.proof: timeline-shared-ticks tests verify identical mapped positions and a throwing time-authority getter proves no duplicate map resolution.
implementation.limits: Standalone ruler callers may omit mapped ticks and retain their independent fallback.

findings.title: Move timeline spectrogram FFT work off the renderer thread
findings.observedWork: Each visible spectrogram column fills FFT input, calls PFFFT, and groups magnitudes synchronously. Whole-buffer analysis is called inside a layout-effect painter; streamed tile analysis also runs synchronously after its read resolves. Bounded PCM memory does not bound renderer-thread CPU per tile.
findings.proposedChange: Run column analysis in a dedicated worker with transferred bounded PCM windows and cancellation/version keys; publish ready raster/columns back to the renderer.
findings.scenario: Switch a long stereo clip to spectrogram/multiview or zoom its FFT window while playing.
findings.validation: Renderer long-task duration and p95 interaction latency during analysis, plus time to final spectrogram and worker transfer bytes.
findings.existingProtection: PFFFT windows/scratch, per-canvas analysis/image cache, streamed bounded tiles, and abort handling already exist; preserve those. This is not a startup import candidate.

implementation.change: Analyze bounded spectrogram PCM tiles in cancellable workers using the unchanged PFFFT engine.
implementation.proof: timeline-spectrogram-worker tests preserve exact band values/context and borrowed PCM ownership, terminate on cancellation;39combined spectrum/row/cache focused tests pass.
implementation.limits: Worker admission covers up to8channels and width32,768; unavailable Worker or unsupported shapes retain the existing exact fallback.

findings.title: Support bulk spectrogram rasterization at fractional backing ratios
findings.observedWork: The ImageData fast path requires integer transform scales and integer rectangle geometry. A fractional devicePixelRatio, fractional clip width, or unequal stereo channel height often fails those checks and falls back to per-frequency-span fillRect writes.
findings.proposedChange: Rasterize directly in backing-pixel coordinates with shared rounded boundaries, or rasterize at logical pixels and draw the cached image at the requested ratio; choose by verified visual parity.
findings.scenario: Spectrogram display in Electron on 125%/150% scaling and asymmetrically sized stereo channels.
findings.validation: Bulk-path hit ratio and canvas calls/paint CPU at fractional DPI, screenshot seam/antialiasing parity.
findings.existingProtection: The bulk painter and cached offscreen images already improve integer-aligned geometry; this targets the remaining fallback cases.

implementation.change: Use bulk ImageData painting at fractional positive backing ratios when every physical rectangle boundary is integral.
implementation.proof: Chromium spectral painter specs compare all pixels across existing scales/stereo geometry and12new aligned fractional-density cases;11Node image-data tests pass. Warm isolated1024×256 example medians ~391ms rectangles /102ms bulk, variable parallel load.
implementation.limits: Arbitrary fractional anti-aliasing remains rectangle-painted: the prior reference semantics cannot be reproduced by assigning whole pixels. Admission checks avoid approximating visual output.

findings.title: Retain reusable fixed spectrogram tiles across viewport shifts
findings.observedWork: Completed tile columns are keyed to the entire projected clip start/end/width. Crossing a render anchor replaces that viewport key, discards completed columns, aborts old jobs, and regenerates the overlapping analysis.
findings.proposedChange: Cache fixed source/time tiles by immutable audio content, FFT/window, and resolution; assemble the current window from retained intersections and analyze only new coverage under a byte-budgeted LRU.
findings.scenario: Slow horizontal scrolling or back-and-forth scrubbing across a long streamed spectrogram.
findings.validation: Overlapping FFT columns recomputed/read bytes per anchor transition and time until a new viewport is painted; cache memory cap.
findings.existingProtection: Within one request key, completed tiles survive visual publications and exact scroll uses render anchors. This targets reuse between distinct anchors, not absence of existing caching.

implementation.change: Retain reusable clip-local FFT columns across anchored viewport windows when the existing sample centers form the same integer grid.
implementation.proof: spectrogram-column-reuse tests shift a256-column view by64columns and analyze only64new columns; repeat view performs zero PCM reads/FFT work. Fresh stereo PFFFT energies with signed gain/nonlinear fades match every cached value exactly.
implementation.limits: Noninteger frame/pixel ratios or different anchor phases change the original FFT centers and are excluded; reusing or resampling those columns would alter spectral values.

findings.title: Bound and prioritize multitrack spectrogram jobs
findings.observedWork: Each mounted row starts every projected clip request immediately, with no scheduler shared across rows. A viewport revealing many spectrogram clips can queue simultaneous reads and analysis, increasing contention and slowing the selected visible clip's response.
findings.proposedChange: Use a controller-owned bounded queue across rows, prioritize selected/onscreen clips over overscan, and cancel superseded jobs before admitting more work.
findings.scenario: Reveal several long spectrogram tracks or change FFT settings across a multitrack view.
findings.validation: Concurrent read/analysis count, selected-clip first/final paint latency, renderer long tasks and peak PCM memory.
findings.existingProtection: Each job uses bounded PCM tiles and AbortController; this candidate only adds cross-job admission/prioritization.

implementation.change: Share a two-active/128-pending priority queue across tracks and cap completed reusable spectral-column retention at32MiB with LRU eviction.
implementation.proof: Bounded queue tests cover priority/cancellation; column-cache tests cover key/array/band/entry accounting, LRU heat, oversized values, controller namespace isolation and empty namespace release; hook tests preserve stale abort and no-partial/no-endless-retry behavior.
implementation.limits: 32MiB is the completed reusable-column retention bound, not total visible working data. Current mounted results retain arrays needed to display their spectra; dropping them at cache eviction would gray/flicker the timeline.

findings.title: Memoize immutable waveform content identity and time authority keys
findings.observedWork: A clip projection serializes content identity, maps its entire envelope, and may serialize a full tempo map before testing a waveform cache hit. It constructs another content identity for cacheSignature; spectrogram request keys serialize overlapping content again.
findings.proposedChange: Cache normalized content identity by immutable clip/source identity and a separate tempo-map revision key; combine scalar window/resolution keys without reserializing whole envelopes/maps.
findings.scenario: Select/scroll warped clips with dense envelope points and large tempo maps.
findings.validation: JSON/string allocations, envelope entries visited per cache hit, projection CPU; mutation-safe fallback for noncanonical callers.
findings.existingProtection: Waveform plans already cache by explicit content signature and object-source identity. Preserve all source/audio/time invalidations while making cache-key construction cheaper.

implementation.change: Memoize exact JSON fragments only for deeply frozen waveform envelope/warp/time-authority inputs.
implementation.proof: waveform-preview-cache/immutable-key tests preserve mutable and shallow-frozen changes while reusing immutable serialization; content/time/FFT changes keep separate spectral keys.
implementation.limits: Mutable inputs deliberately serialize each time to preserve invalidation.

findings.title: Index authored automation points and visible spans during overlay projection
findings.observedWork: Each clip scans all automation points twice to find its authored points. Each generated curve sample additionally findIndex-scans those points to discover hold boundaries; Bezier handles scan every projected span to test visibility.
findings.proposedChange: Build one frame-to-point-index map, range-query sorted point frames, and binary-query merged visible spans for handles.
findings.scenario: Render or drag a lane with thousands of authored points across many clips.
findings.validation: Point/span comparisons per overlay projection, CPU and allocations; preserve duplicate-position/hold-transition behavior.
findings.existingProtection: Lane normalization compiles/caches interpolation curves, so do not claim interpolation recompiles per sample. The remaining scans occur in the visual projector.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed repeated linear scans; impact unmeasured

implementation.change: Retain authored automation point/frame indexes and query visible spans without repeated whole-lane scans.
implementation.proof: automation-frame-index tests preserve rounded-frame collision semantics, predecessor/successor anchors and indexed visibility;14automation geometry tests pass.
implementation.limits: An edited lane or changed time authority rebuilds its index.

findings.title: Use compact segment geometry for simple automation curves
findings.observedWork: Even a constant lane/current value emits samples every two CSS pixels, freezes sample objects, and creates a long SVG path. This work is unnecessary for constant spans; linear or hold segments can often be represented by endpoints under a linear descriptor taper.
findings.proposedChange: Emit exact minimal geometry for constant/hold/linear-in-screen-space segments and use error-bounded adaptive subdivision for nonlinear taper/eased/Bezier segments.
findings.scenario: Wide timeline with automation overlay enabled on several nearly constant tracks.
findings.validation: Sample objects/path bytes per span, overlay CPU and SVG paint time; numerical pixel-error threshold and exact hold corners.
findings.existingProtection: The current fixed two-pixel sampling bounds visual density; replacement must retain nonlinear curve/taper accuracy rather than simply reducing quality.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed oversampling of constant spans; impact unmeasured

implementation.change: Use anchor-only geometry for constant/linear absolute automation and adaptive error-bounded eased/Bezier geometry.
implementation.proof: automation-sample-frames tests reduce a501-point constant span to2anchors and validate eased geometry against dense evaluation within quarter-pixel error with fewer than150points.
implementation.limits: Musical curves retain the existing authoritative2CSS-pixel sampling because tempo mapping changes screen/value geometry; adaptive spans retain recursion/gap/error caps.

findings.title: Limit automation draft normalization and React publication to one per frame

findings.title: Select track meter display values instead of entire telemetry objects
findings.observedWork: Track/output meters subscribe to full meter objects with Object.is, although their display only uses dbfs and peak clipping. A fresh object with spectrum/RMS/loudness changes can rerender these components despite identical rendered values.

findings.observedWork: Live mixer fills update top; ordinary horizontal/vertical meters update width/height and peak-marker left/bottom through CSS variables. These properties require layout/paint rather than a transform-only update.

findings.title: Run long built-in generators off the renderer thread
findings.observedWork: generateSignal calls synchronous generateAudioEditorSignal before the first storage await; markProcessing is not called until line 273. All tone, chirp, noise and DTMF sample loops therefore block the renderer and even delay the busy feedback.

findings.scenario: Generate several minutes of stereo pink noise while dragging the timeline or attempting Cancel in Electron with speed preference.
findings.validation: Click-to-first-busy-paint, renderer long-task maximum, dropped animation frames, and click-to-committed-generated-clip p50/p95.
findings.correctness: Preserve deterministic seed sequence, exact PCM and channel order, project/task ownership and transactional source publication.

implementation.proof: Root generator worker/controller tests; Electron generation now runs DSP outside renderer; parent owns end-to-end metrics. findings.title: Generate bounded PCM blocks instead of materializing the complete signal
findings.observedWork: generateFixedDuration allocates the entire duration; generator-service retains all channels while createBuffer subsequently copies them. Generation supports up to 24 hours subject to frame bounds.
findings.proposedChange: Give each generator a stateful block iterator (phase, noise bins/RNG, segment offset) that writes bounded blocks and feeds incremental peak construction, with backpressure.
findings.scenario: Generate a long chirp or noise selection that creates large arrays and GC pauses before publication.
findings.validation: Peak process RSS, allocated PCM bytes, longest renderer task and Generate-to-clip latency for 30 s, 5 min and 30 min inputs.
findings.correctness: Chunk partitions must yield the same seeded PCM and segment boundaries as the one-shot result. Coordinate with existing chunked writers; this is a generator producer change.

implementation.change: Generate bounded PCM blocks instead of materializing the complete signal
implementation.proof: Pinned exact hashes at block sizes 1/127/128/129/257/4096, adaptive blocks, transfer detachment, 32 channels/seeds, and two-hour generation with bounded allocations. findings.validation: Copied bytes and allocation count: one fewer frameCount*4 buffer for every such generation; exact channel independence regression.

implementation.limits: Exact numerical behavior and existing ownership/cancellation contracts retained.

findings.observedWork: Each occurrence of a digit recomputes two Math.sin calls and the same fade envelope for every frame; its phase resets to zero on every occurrence.

findings.title: Retain a bounded selection/spectral worker pool across successful operations
findings.observedWork: Each apply constructs a new selection worker; executeWorker cleanup terminates it even on success at line 333. PFFFT ready/plans and the StaffPad runtime promise are per-worker module caches and disappear with it.

findings.scenario: Apply several short EQ/noise-reduction/change-tempo effects, or run multiple offline macro steps.
findings.validation: Warm repeated Apply latency, worker creations, WASM instantiations and FFT-plan creations per operation.
findings.correctness: Keep memory bounded, reset deterministic DSP/RNG state and ownership between jobs, and preserve hard cancellation/timeout/error semantics.

findings.title: Transfer consumed dry-effect buffers without another full PCM clone
findings.observedWork: cloneAudacityWorkerPayload Float32Array.from-copies all selection and context channels before transferring them. renderDryTrackRange already returns newly rendered channel arrays, so some one-shot paths have no remaining reader for that PCM.
findings.proposedChange: Introduce an explicit owned/consumed-buffer request path that transfers exclusively owned dry/context buffers directly; keep cloning for preview caches, borrowed source data, linked jobs or fallback paths.
findings.scenario: Apply an effect to a multi-minute stereo selection, including EQ preroll.
findings.validation: Renderer clone time, copied bytes, peak RSS and click-to-result latency.
findings.correctness: Never detach cached AudioBuffer storage, retained history, source PCM, control buffers reused by another target or a preview cache. Ownership must be proven by API contract.

implementation.change: Transfer consumed dry-effect buffers without another full PCM clone
implementation.proof: Root transfer ownership tests validate exact-span fresh buffers and consumption. Cached retained PCM is cloned before transfer.
implementation.limits: Exact numerical behavior and existing ownership/cancellation contracts retained.

findings.title: Process independent target tracks through bounded concurrent jobs
findings.observedWork: All target dry renders finish serially before processing starts, then each target effect worker is awaited serially at lines 182–211. Independent tracks do not overlap render/DSP work.
findings.proposedChange: Use a memory-budgeted pipeline with a small worker/render concurrency limit; retain input order and commit all targets atomically. Keep shared-peak parameter resolution and linked truncate-silence as barriers.
findings.scenario: Apply EQ, noise reduction or compressor to several selected independent tracks on a multicore Electron machine.
findings.validation: Total Apply latency, CPU utilization, peak RSS, per-target completion times and renderer frame gaps at 1/2/4 concurrent jobs.
findings.correctness: The current worker service cancels a prior selection job, so it needs multiple isolated owners rather than Promise.all around the current API. Linked effects and aggregate parameter analysis cannot be split freely.

implementation.change: Speed-mode, canonical-owned independent selection targets use a bounded pool of two private selection worker lanes. Target context is prepared in original order, replies stay in target order, workers remain warm, and queued dispatches fence current project authority.
implementation.proof: Three pool TDD tests prove a maximum of two lanes, opposite completion order, cancellation/supersession of both lanes, safe new ordinary-job completion, and no queued work after stale ownership. Existing warm-worker, transfer, macro and selection-worker contract tests pass; focused ESLint and complete source/tests TypeScript pass. Cross-review reproduced a pending-EQ-preflight supersession race red. Regression proves batch/single/explicit cancel/caller abort reject the old request before delayed WASM resolves, then old continuation cannot allocate a third worker or cancel newer lanes. Ordinary cancellation is forwarded through preflight and raced to release UI ownership immediately. Two-lane stalled-EQ regression additionally proves canceled batch rejection precedes shared WASM resolution and that delayed continuations cannot affect the newer ordinary job. The private owner race leaves shared module loading alive; 31 focused worker/pool/chain tests and targeted ESLint pass.
implementation.limits: The existing peak calculation sums every target PCM/context/DSP workspace before dispatch. Linked Truncate Silence retains its one shared worker request; headless/untrusted/memory-mode ports stay serial. This closes a source-cost candidate; no claimed Electron percentage.

findings.title: Render effect selection and neighboring context in one extended range
findings.observedWork: The selection is rendered at lines 140–149, then preroll and postroll each call renderDryTrackRange again at lines 197 and 202, constructing separate isolated snapshots and offline renders.
findings.proposedChange: Plan one extended dry range per target and split its owned PCM into before/selection/after views; retain the exact original start/end and requested clip scope.
findings.scenario: Apply parametric EQ (10-second preroll), Repair (128-sample selection), or StaffPad pitch/tempo changes.
findings.validation: Offline render/context constructions per target: up to three→one; Apply latency especially for tiny repaired ranges.
findings.correctness: Preserve boundary padding, authored clip fades and channel mapping. An extended render must not accidentally include neighboring clips outside requestedClipIds.

implementation.change: Render effect selection and neighboring context in one extended range
implementation.proof: Coalesced context tests plus execution integration: one admitted read vs three legacy reads, independent exact-span transferable outputs, and memory headroom fallback.

findings.title: Reuse immutable neighbor context across offline macro steps
findings.observedWork: Every context-requiring offline step renders before/after PCM again through renderNeighbouringRange, although the documented neighbors remain authored project audio and are unchanged by the chain.
findings.proposedChange: Keep a per-run, per-target cache of bounded neighboring dry PCM keyed by track/clip scope/range/channels and captured project revision; a larger context can serve smaller slices.
findings.scenario: Run a macro with several EQ, Repair or StaffPad steps over the same target.
findings.validation: Neighbor renders and copied context bytes per chain; macro Apply latency.
findings.correctness: Share only unchanged neighboring PCM, never the evolving selection; retain project ownership and bound cache lifetime to the macro run.

implementation.change: Reuse immutable neighbor context across offline macro steps
implementation.proof: 28 macro tests include exact evolving selection PCM, repeated Repair read count4→2, malicious worker mutation cannot poison cached neighbors, fresh second run, cancellation and zero/tight-budget fallback.
implementation.limits: 4MiB maximum, one macro-run lifetime, only immutable neighbor windows; selection PCM is always processed anew.

findings.title: Run consecutive offline macro steps inside one worker request
findings.observedWork: Each offline step crosses runtime.runSelectionEffect, returning PCM to the renderer before the next step clones/transfers it back into a freshly created worker.
findings.proposedChange: Dispatch an offline segment as an ordered list of steps with its immutable context; keep intermediate owned PCM inside one worker and transfer only the final result.
findings.scenario: Run a macro containing normalize→noise reduction→fade or several destructive effects.
findings.validation: Worker round trips, intermediate PCM transferred/copied bytes, worker creations and macro click-to-result time.
findings.correctness: Preserve step order, shared parameter semantics, length changes, error identity, cancellation and the existing single undo/transactional publication.

implementation.change: A private worker packet retains current PCM across up to 32 consecutive context-free offline Audacity macro steps, performing the original channel matching after every individual effect. Longer eligible segments split into bounded packets.
implementation.proof: Exact actual DSP comparison for mono/stereo fade, repeat, reverse, Amplify and Normalize preserves Float32 bytes, length changes and per-step matching; synthetic signed-zero/subnormal and layout tests also pass. Segment tests prove 35 steps split 32+3, Repair barrier, serial public-port fallback, and stale ownership. Headless cancellation is fenced per step; worker validated sequential step completion resets the original per-step deadline, while duplicate/out-of-order messages cannot extend it. 43 effect/macro/worker tests and 61 targeted/chunk-owner tests pass; source/tests TypeScript and focused ESLint pass.
implementation.limits: Speed production port only. Realtime racks, control/neighbor/StaffPad/noise-profile context, reviewed authorization, unknown effect types and custom public matching ports keep their existing separate execution. Existing per-step DSP validation/normalization/RNG and canonical one-result persistence remain. No intermediate engine re-render existed between the original consecutive offline steps.

findings.title: Slice already-rendered full-selection PCM for short previews

findings.observedWork: Amplify preparation renders the entire selection for its default gain; Apply rerenders it at line 141. Preview also renders its own dry selection and no reusable revision-keyed dry-result cache is retained by these services.

implementation.proof: 25 preparation/service/gain tests cover private copy ownership, one-time consumption, canonical identity changes, project scope abort, Speed opt-in and memory headroom fallback.

findings.observedWork: applyAudacityEffectAsync awaits initializePffft for every non-StaffPad Audacity effect, including Amplify, Invert, fades, DC removal, echo and compressor whose implementations perform no FFT.

findings.title: Use a direct dry-PCM path for simple unprocessed selections

implementation.proof: 12 actual Chromium engine comparisons bit-exact at8k/44.1k/48k/96k, requested offsets/padding/-0/subnormals;22 service/folder tests preserve non-neutral fallback.

findings.title: Index engine render-range clip plans and retain crossfade preparation
findings.observedWork: Every render rebuilds a map of all project clips, obtains every clip in each active track, prepares automatic crossfades for all track clips, then checks range intersection in the inner loop. The timeline viewport index does not serve this engine scheduler.
findings.proposedChange: Prepare immutable engine snapshot indexes once, query only clips intersecting the render range (including long overlaps), and reuse canonical per-track crossfade geometry until affected clips change.
findings.scenario: Apply or Preview a tiny selection in an hour-long project containing thousands of clips; repeated short renders use the same document.
findings.validation: Authored clip geometry reads and crossfade sorts per range render, scheduler preparation milliseconds and Apply latency.
findings.correctness: Include crossfade relationships involving clips outside the requested range; preserve source-resolution, exact authored ordering, loop/warp expansion and arbitrary mutable caller fallback.

implementation.change: Frozen data-owned clip geometry is prepared once per immutable project. Validated per-track membership, full-track automatic crossfades and interval prefix-end indexes query only overlapping clips while preserving original schedule and summing order.
implementation.proof: Exact uncached/current indexed plans across duplicate IDs, overlapping/nested/zero-length/boundary/NaN/Infinity queries; mutable membership, live source resolution and poisoned returned ranges remain correct. Second 1000-clip narrow render geometry reads drop from 4000 to 4. Standalone 10000-clip warm median 10.3152ms uncached vs 0.0555ms retained (/tmp/soundscaper-clip-schedule-kernels.json), exact six-window plan comparisons. 33 helper/engine/warp/crossfade/lifecycle tests pass; focused ESLint and complete source/tests TypeScript pass.
implementation.limits: Only frozen root/frozen data-property clip geometry is indexed; mutable/accessor generic inputs preserve original uncached authority. Track membership is checked each query, media/warp/source resolution remains live. At most 32768 retained clip entries and 64 tracks per project; public plans own fresh crossfade ranges. Timing is a schedule kernel, not Electron end-to-end or arbitrary graph rendering.

findings.title: Replace large-export realtime fallback with bounded faster-than-realtime rendering

implementation.change: Export opts into a bounded faster-than-realtime offline renderer for admitted stateless neutral single-clip stereo graphs.

findings.title: Feed offline compressed encoders bounded PCM without a complete staging WAV
findings.observedWork: The full admitted render is synchronously encodeWav-ed into one Uint8Array and then one Blob before encodeDirectCompressedStagedFile begins.
findings.proposedChange: Extend the existing desktop streaming codec contract to accept render PCM blocks directly, applying the admitted conversion/dither once; avoid the complete WAV encode/Blob/decode/reinterleave cycle.

implementation.change: Desktop-only prepared PCM producer streams final mapped/resampled float blocks through existing bundled encoder protocol without intermediate WAV staging.
implementation.proof: 53 targeted runtime/export/custody tests and 29 ownership assertions; actual legacy WAV carrier vs direct PCM byte parity after custom mapping and 44.1→48kHz resampling. 40k stereo input in 313 render quanta coalesces to 3 acknowledged native packets. Cancel/plan drift stops after first ACK; malformed or unacknowledged producer geometry drains safely before cleanup. Root extracted packet writer to remove architecture cycle; mapping supported in 0afacbe89.
implementation.limits: Exact bundled non-FLAC final float geometry only; external/nativeAAC/browser and integerFLAC use established staging. Existing closed native plan, output validation, range custody and canonical save destination are reused. No native runtime bytes changed; no manual AI asset update.

findings.title: Pipeline independent stem render and ordered archive emission
findings.observedWork: Each stem fully awaits renderStem and archive.add before the following stem starts.
findings.proposedChange: Use a memory-admitted pipeline with at most one next stem render/encode in progress while the previous completed stem drains into the sequential archive. Retain deterministic archive order.
findings.scenario: Export 16 independent short stems to a ZIP on a desktop with spare cores and a relatively slow destination disk.
findings.validation: Complete archive latency, encoder/renderer/disk overlap, peak staged bytes, archive order and CRC equality.
findings.existingProtection: Current sequential path intentionally stages only one render and has hard byte contracts; keep that path on memory-constrained hosts.
findings.correctness: May provide little gain for shared single-thread codec contention; benchmark before enabling concurrency. Preserve abort cleanup for the speculative next stem.

implementation.change: For admitted native same-rate multi-stem direct ZIP/7z exports in Speed mode, render/conform at most one following entry while the current archive entry is written. One active render and at most current+next owned outputs; deterministic archive order. Private per-entry phase/cancellation adapters preserve the owning export task, and one export-wide absolute adapter keeps raw observer progress monotonic. The default snapshot factory explicitly creates compatible owned-entry renderers; custom supplied renderers without that capability stay sequential. implementation.proof: 75 focused tests pass across direct ZIP/native 7z/compressed sequential contracts, service, deferred facade and semantic chunk ownership; 17 new focused tests pass. Controlled archive backpressure shows Speed starts stem two before stem-one write ACK, while Memory waits; actual encodeWav ZIP output matches sequential exact bytes/order. Private offline failures retry through the real streaming WAV encoder and same-rate resampler with exact ZIP parity, two staging removes and two renderer disposals. Real createExportPlan short 48kHz stereo two-stem plan admits with entry384044B, archive768350B, retry384000B, heap19465304B and combined temporary1920438B under unchanged desktop thresholds. Mutable preflight aborts before any renderer; protocol tests cover bounded outputs, cancellation, late successful spool cleanup, and both nested AggregateError orderings. npm run lint:changed, explicit owned-file ESLint, source tsc, full tests tsc and latest-three-test strict typing pass; size and whitespace checks pass.
implementation.limits: Native WAV/BWF/AIFF direct archives only, at least two entries, each encoded entry <=32MiB; same source/output rate, existing offline fast/admitted plan, Speed preference and compatible owned resources required. Loudness normalization, binaural/mastering/ADM graphs, Memory/unknown preference, custom renderer without owned-entry capability, rate conversion and capacity failures remain sequential. Combined storage includes full archive + two encoded entries + source-width retry F32 spool; summed heap thresholds unchanged. Overlap proven using controlled write backpressure and exact bytes; no measured end-to-end Electron speedup claimed. No UI entry changes, codec ABI changes or assistance-runtime closure changes; manual Update AI assets is not required.

findings.title: Let Speed publish lossless raw PCM before optional compression
findings.observedWork: Every persistent write calls pcm.encode(packPlanarFloat32(...)) and awaits compression before OPFS/IndexedDB write and source commit. optimizeFor is not consulted here.
findings.proposedChange: Under desktop Speed, write supported raw-f32le chunks immediately and schedule atomic low-priority lossless compression/replacement after the result is usable, subject to storage capacity.
findings.scenario: Apply a destructive effect to a ten-minute recording or accept a large generated enhancement result.
findings.validation: Apply-to-visible-result latency, first playable result, encoder CPU time, background interference, raw/compressed exact PCM equality and crash/reopen durability.

findings.correctness: Requires careful capacity admission, exact-generation replacement and history/retention fences; do not let background replacement change source identity silently.

Independent final review adds conversion/verification/binding cleanup regressions; 51 focused consolidation tests pass. Linked-audio cache writes also retain simultaneous write/abort failures; 17 linked/managed tests pass.

findings.title: Remove the second raw PCM ownership copy before WavPack encode

findings.title: Use private channel views for owned decoded planar PCM
findings.observedWork: On little-endian hosts unpackPlanarFloat32 slices the owned decoded payload separately for every channel.

implementation.proof: PCM checksum tests cover private sharing, source/input mutation isolation, fresh subsequent reads and unavailable-worker fallback.

findings.title: Move PCM checksum work off the renderer hot path
findings.observedWork: PCM encode computes a byte-by-byte JS CRC32 before its worker call; decode also recomputes CRC32 in renderer at lines 177/207. wavpack/pcm.js:139-146 is a scalar loop.
findings.proposedChange: Compute and validate identical CRC32 in a worker/native byte-processing stage that owns the payload, returning an authenticated exact-geometry result; preserve all corruption checks.
findings.scenario: Persist/read long multichannel PCM while keeping the timeline responsive.
findings.validation: Renderer CPU and long tasks, CRC worker time, p95 read/write latency and corruption fixtures. Reproduce the isolated CRC cost with scripts/performance/measure-pcm-helpers.mjs; retain every trial, including GC/shared-host variation, in editing-performance-measurements.json.

implementation.proof: CRC worker transfers do not fetch WASM; decoded corruption is rejected, abort propagates, unavailable workers retain independent main-thread CRC fallback.
implementation.limits: Memory-mode encode still computes its baseline CRC in renderer; worker transport and fallback can retain copies.

findings.title: Replace per-chunk full ancestry metadata scans with a coherent generation fence
findings.observedWork: Every read calls assertGenerationCurrent before and after chunk access; that loops serial getMetadata over every COW ancestor at lines 204-209.
findings.proposedChange: Acquire an exact-generation read lease or a transaction-coherent generation version at session admission, invalidate it when any retained ancestor changes, and keep cheap per-read fence checks.

findings.existingProtection: Session admission already captures the ancestry and validates it; current repeated checks deliberately protect exact source identity.
findings.correctness: Cannot cache only metadata timestamps or omit currentness checks; needs an authoritative invalidation/lease mechanism.

implementation.proof: 57 ancestry/read tests; replacement, cancellation and release guards preserved; cap4094 generations.
implementation.limits: No authoritative cross-edit invalidation lease exists, so all-ancestor comparisons remain on every packet.

findings.title: Memoize which COW generation owns each chunk
findings.observedWork: After generation checks, each read probes records.chunk on successive COW ancestors until a replacement or physical base is found.

findings.scenario: Repeated playback/render of an unchanged region after100 sparse edits far from that region. Applicable after the resident source buffer cache is exceeded or evicted; short fully resident sources may bypass this path.

implementation.limits: Owner/absence memoization is deliberately not used because same-generation chunk insertion would make cached owners stale.

findings.title: Allow bounded concurrent positional reads of immutable PCM
findings.observedWork: One queue serializes all chunk calls in a session even when chunk indexes are independent.
findings.proposedChange: Offer a bounded positional-read session for backends that safely support it, allowing disk I/O for the next packet while the current one decodes/consumes. Keep serialization for stateful/non-positional backends.
findings.scenario: A long render or assistance preparation on fast SSD with multiple independent PCM chunks. Applicable after the resident source buffer cache is exceeded or evicted; short fully resident sources may bypass this path.
findings.validation: Storage-read overlap, chunk throughput, maximum in-flight bytes, cancellation latency and release/error ordering tests.
findings.existingProtection: Single-file lifetime and request-local cancellation are already well modeled; do not remove those guarantees.

The parsed canonical packet geometry admits two only when encoded input plus two decoded representations for both packets fit64MiB.

findings.title: Reuse an OPFS source readable within an exact-generation session
findings.observedWork: readPcmContainerChunk reacquires sourceFile each time; sourceFile may ask sync.readable or getFileHandle/getFile at lines 417-422. Container indexes are cached separately.

findings.title: Read a legacy multichannel PCM chunk as one bounded byte span

implementation.change: Read all legacy multichannel PCM for one chunk as one bounded span.

implementation.limits: Applies to legacy raw OPFS, not modern indexed containers.

findings.title: Avoid coalescer copies for already aligned owned PCM packets
findings.observedWork: The coalescer allocates pendingChannels and copies all samples even when a full input packet exactly matches chunkFrames and no pending tail exists.

findings.correctness: Emitted chunks are consumer-owned; directly forwarding borrowed decoder scratch buffers would corrupt output.

implementation.change: Owned full aligned coalescer packets pass through without pending-buffer copies; writeBuffer supplies fresh private slices.
implementation.proof: 15 coalescer/source tests; owned identity and backpressure, borrowed and partial copy isolation, history-safe writeBuffer private identity.
implementation.limits: Fast path requires explicit owned input; borrowed decoder buffers and partial boundaries keep copying.

findings.title: Stream desktop compressed decode into canonical PCM storage
findings.observedWork: decode materializes all input with boundedInputBytes, sends a whole Uint8Array request, receives complete output and projects it. IPC permits64 MiB total active input at desktop-audio-codec-main-ipc.ts:62.

findings.scenario: Import a long MP3/FLAC or multichannel compressed recording after the editor is ready.
findings.validation: Import-to-first-visible/playable source latency, total import wall time, peak RSS, renderer long tasks and sample/gapless conformance.
findings.existingProtection: Desktop encode has streaming support; this candidate is specifically the remaining buffered decode API.

findings.title: Detach only changed immutable project branches for publication

An alternative is a trusted command change-set for incrementally updating the detached view. Keep full detachment for untrusted/mutable inputs.

findings.validation: Visited/copied snapshot nodes and allocated bytes per small edit, snapshot build CPU, command-to-visible-result p50/p95, retained cache bytes.

Preserve proxy detachment, cyclic identity, read-only Map/Set behavior and capability branding. This requires immutable update ownership, not a blind global WeakMap.

Alternating warmed exact-baseline command probe deepEqual verifies all metadata, mixer, automation, revisions and timestamps;1000 clips50.81→37.96ms,2000 clips96.40→74.94ms.

findings.title: Retain effect-type catalog snapshots for each registry and locale
findings.observedWork: Every document publication remaps the rack and selection effect registries into fresh frozen objects, recomputes hasSettings using Object.keys, and obtains a fresh video-definition array even when the registry/copy has not changed.

findings.validation: Registry mapping/Object.keys invocations and effect-catalog allocations per publication; snapshot build CPU and dependent menu renders.

implementation.proof: Published-snapshot and document-snapshot tests preserve frozen public snapshots and caller input isolation; mutable external input fallback recomputes.
implementation.limits: Only production composition opts into immutable generations; no blind cache of arbitrary mutable objects.

findings.title: Reuse admitted preset normalization and per-effect lists
findings.observedWork: Every document snapshot calls listAudioEditorEffectPresets, which normalizes every saved preset, checks ID uniqueness and freezes another normalized state before filtering for the current effect and appending factory presets. Unrelated project/status publications repeat this work over the whole library.
findings.proposedChange: Retain normalization at an explicit admission boundary for an immutable preset-state identity, and cache its display list by preset revision/current effect/factory registry revision. Keep validation for arbitrary imported or mutable inputs.
findings.scenario: Use a large imported user-preset library, then apply several effects or update selections without changing that library.
findings.validation: Preset normalizations and allocated parameter objects per publish, snapshot build CPU at 100/1,000/5,000 saved presets, preset-menu render counts.
findings.existingProtection: Preset CRUD returns frozen normalized states. This must not bypass import/type/timestamp/duplicate-ID validation or assume arbitrary caller objects are immutable.

findings.title: Retain detached macro and script libraries until their revision changes
findings.observedWork: Every snapshot recursively materializes and freezes the entire macro library and script library using a fresh traversal map, although their services replace library state only on explicit library edits/imports. Unlike preferences and project lists, these potentially large detached values have no retained publication identity.
findings.proposedChange: Cache detached macros/scripts by the controller-owned immutable library identity or explicit revision; return a stable frozen empty value. Invalidate on import/save/delete and preserve mutation isolation.

implementation.limits: Persistence, import, update and delete replace list ownership and invalidate derived script data.

findings.title: Batch synchronous controller presentation transitions into one publication
