Suppress identical status replacements. Preserve an initial busy publication before expensive work begins.
findings.scenario: Analyze a short selection, repeat a cached analysis, or finish several macro/effect steps that update result/status/busy together.
findings.validation: Snapshot builds/subscriber notifications per operation and build CPU; busy-first-paint and final-result latency; cancellation/stale-owner tests.
findings.existingProtection: Realtime telemetry already has a separate channel. Do not defer busy state across the compute phase or allow an older task's finish to clear a newer task's busy flag.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed duplicate synchronous build path; React frame impact unmeasured

implementation.change: Batch synchronous start and completion publications for analysis, generation and ordinary Audacity Apply; nested scopes release on exceptions.
implementation.proof: Snapshot-channel/composition tests plus generation and analysis completion regressions verify one batch owns result/success/idle transitions and stale tasks cannot release newer busy state. Initial busy publication remains before expensive work. Ordinary Apply regression proves success/last-effect/idle share one batch;31 worker tests cover prompt cancellation and supersession during shared EQ preflight.
implementation.limits: No scope spans an await. Progress, specialized partial results and the outer task-progress owner remain separately observable; Nyquist and macro transitions are not all batched.

findings.title: Publish the requested specialized analysis before independent generic metrics finish
findings.observedWork: Plot Spectrum and Find Clipping await renderAndAnalyze, including complete EBU/true-peak/generic metrics, before starting their independent report computation. The specialized report cannot become visible until both serial phases finish.
findings.proposedChange: After the single authored mix render, start specialized reporting and generic metrics as independent owned tasks; publish the specialized report as soon as ready, then publish the completed generic metrics/visuals. Retain all existing metrics and disable/export or mark incomplete payloads until they are complete.
findings.scenario: Plot spectrum or find clipping on a long selection where generic loudness and true-peak processing dominate the requested report's first-result latency.
findings.validation: Click-to-specialized-report first paint versus click-to-complete-analysis, total CPU, extra buffer bytes and renderer frame gaps; report equality and project-change cancellation.
findings.existingProtection: Generic analysis already executes in a worker. AnalysisPanel currently shows generic metrics in every mode and exports result+report, so eliminating that work would change behavior. This is scheduling/progressive publication, not deletion of required metrics. Contrast needs RMS first and should only use this after preserving exact generic RMS semantics.
findings.correctness: Bind partial and complete metrics/report/visuals to the same request and revision; clear or mark previous generic metrics while partial results are displayed. Preserve the complete export contract.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed serial dependency; first-result benefit unmeasured

implementation.change: Run specialized spectrum/clipping reporting and generic metrics independently after one authored render; publish specialized reports as soon as ready.
implementation.proof: Analysis tests hold generic metrics pending and observe the specialized report with previous metrics cleared; both complete before final report caching/export.
implementation.limits: Render remains shared and single-owner; generic metrics still run, and partial results cannot be exported.

findings.title: Persist completed analysis after displaying the result
findings.observedWork: On a levels-analysis cache miss, the complete result and visuals are ready but the service awaits cache persistence before showAnalysis. Slow analysis-store writes delay result visibility; a cache write failure prevents the computed report from being shown.
findings.proposedChange: Assert ownership and publish the complete result first, then schedule bounded tracked cache persistence outside the display critical path with captured revision/key and explicit failure handling. Preserve flush/disposal semantics where required.
findings.scenario: Analyze a selection while the project's storage backend is busy writing PCM or autosave data.
findings.validation: Time from DSP completion to analysis first paint, injected cache-write latency versus UI completion, persistence queue depth and retry/error behavior.
findings.existingProtection: A revision/scope/range levels cache already exists. This preserves its contents and admission checks while removing successful cache persistence from the visible-result dependency.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed critical-path await; storage-delay impact depends on backend

implementation.change: Display computed levels before awaiting cache persistence.
implementation.proof: Controlled pending cache-write regression observes current levels while storage is unresolved, and existing ownership tests reject stale results.
implementation.limits: The tracked analysis task still awaits persistence for deterministic disposal/failure handling; completion and success follow the write.

findings.title: Run spectrum, clipping and delivery loudness reporting off the renderer
findings.observedWork: After rendering, specialized spectrum averages every half-overlapping FFT window synchronously; clipping scans every sample synchronously; Measure Loudness calls synchronous EBU measurement. These direct calls run in the renderer despite generic levels analysis already having a worker implementation.
findings.proposedChange: Extend a bounded analysis worker protocol with specialized report jobs, ordered chunking/backpressure and cancellation; keep numerical reporting algorithms unchanged. Borrow/copy/transfer PCM according to explicit ownership, since the same channels may feed generic metrics and visuals.
findings.scenario: Plot spectrum with a large FFT on a multi-minute mix, Find Clipping on many channels, or Measure Loudness while the timeline is playing.
findings.validation: Renderer long-task maximum and p95 animation frame interval during each analyzer, click-to-report latency, worker CPU and peak memory; exact bins/regions/loudness equivalence.
findings.existingProtection: analyzeChannelsInWorker already offloads generic peak/RMS/EBU work and copies bounded chunks. Do not claim generic analysis lacks a worker, and do not detach buffers still needed by another analysis/visual consumer.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed synchronous sample/FFT loops; Electron trace needed

implementation.change: Compute specialized reports and loudness in an owned cancellable worker.
implementation.proof: Analysis report protocol tests preserve numerical spectrum/clipping/loudness results and worker cancellation/error ownership. Browser and Node fallbacks preserve lazy analysis module ownership.
implementation.limits: Input is copied rather than consumed because generic metrics/visuals share PCM; non-worker environments use established local algorithms.

findings.title: Cache specialized reports by authored content and normalized analysis options
findings.observedWork: The levels path uses a project/revision/scope/track/range cache, while spectrum, clipping and loudness commands always rerender and recompute. Repeating an unchanged specialized request pays the full offline rendering, generic analysis and report cost again.
findings.proposedChange: Use a bounded revision-keyed complete-report cache for spectrum/clipping/loudness, including normalized effective FFT size, threshold/consecutive count, selected scope, ADM weighting and relevant render/runtime settings. Reuse the generic results/visuals where keys match. Validate admission before lookup and invalidate on any audible-content/settings change.
findings.scenario: Repeat Analysis or manually run the same spectrum/clipping report repeatedly on an unchanged selection, or measure unchanged delivery loudness twice.
findings.validation: Offline renders and sample/FFT passes per identical repeat, repeat click-to-report p50/p95, cache hit rate/bytes and invalidation correctness.
findings.existingProtection: Levels caching is already implemented, and the inspector deduplicates automatic requests for the same content key while mounted. This addresses explicit repeats and mode/report reuse; it does not claim automatic duplicates occur on every render.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed absent specialized cache; benefit workload-dependent

implementation.change: Cache one complete spectrum/clipping result with generic metrics/visuals, and one tiny loudness report, under exact authored generation/revision, range/scope/track and effective options.
implementation.proof: Repeated spectrum/clipping tests skip a second render/report job. Three TDD tests failed on prior implementation then pass: repeated exact request invokes render/measurement once, report mutation cannot poison private snapshot, revisions/generations/ranges/sample rate/master width/ADM weight changes miss, ninth-channel input is refused, cancellation cannot publish cache and clears it. Production composition cache and missing-source refusal regression passes. Prior19 loudness/composition tests passed; latest10 focused cache/composition tests passed and focused type-aware lint passed.
implementation.limits: Only one small report is retained, with a WeakRef to generation and no audio buffers. No wall-time or Electron responsiveness measurement claimed. Sources must be immutable under the production generation authority; absent authority disables caching. Root owns app.js grouped wiring commit and canonical types/full gates.

findings.title: Retain command projections within the admitted immutable controller document
findings.observedWork: Each controller command read calls the product command projection again. Soundscaper validates the complete canonical document, then resolves and freezes all timeline clips, tracks, project-bin clips and annotations. Runtime projection branding only avoids resolving an already projected result; the controller reader does not retain that result for its unchanged canonical identity.
findings.proposedChange: Memoize the product command/runtime projection in the controller reader for the admitted immutable project identity (plus any projection-relevant runtime policy), invalidating on document replacement. Retain uncached validation for arbitrary mutable external inputs and preserve product-owned extension fields.
findings.scenario: Several command consumers/enablement queries or repeated edit setup against the same large current document before its next mutation.
findings.validation: Canonical validation/projection invocations and projected clip allocations per current identity, controller preparation CPU and command-to-result latency on 10,000-100,000 clips.
findings.existingProtection: The resolver already shares one coordinate context within a projection and branded runtime projections pass through unchanged. This adds cross-query reuse under controller ownership; a global identity cache for arbitrary mutable projects would be incorrect.
findings.evidenceLevel: code-confirmed repeated projection entry point; representative query frequency/impact unmeasured

implementation.change: Memoize production command/runtime projections at the controller's immutable authored-project reader.
implementation.proof: Controller query and runtime-projection boundary tests preserve product fields and read identity; public mutable/untrusted inputs retain fresh validation.
implementation.limits: Only admitted controller-owned immutable generations reuse projections; project replacement invalidates.
Unimplemented work is explicit in each partial/rejected record; 100 completed optimizations are not claimed. No native AI engine/archive closure changed.

supplementalImprovements.change: A private frozen ordered index precomputes the seven dynamic action templates, avoiding repeated enumeration and parsing of 381 manifest definitions. Public results, parameters, handlers and menus retain fresh caller ownership.
supplementalImprovements.proof: TDD observes 2,000 manifest enumerations before and zero after; 36 focused tests, 1,613 exact before/after matching cases and 841 independently checked adversarial cases pass. Two sets of nine alternating warmed trials are retained in the implementation measurements.
supplementalImprovements.limits: This removes measured renderer publication work. Isolated lookup timings do not establish a whole-operation speedup or explain the entire observed Tone regression.
